title: "Context Engineering"
description: "The design and assembly of the information supplied to a model for a task."
term: "Context Engineering"
letter: "C"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Context engineering is the work of deciding what information an AI model
receives, how it is organized, and when it is provided. Useful context may
include instructions, user input, retrieved documents, conversation
history, and tool results.

## Technical explanation

Context engineering encompasses context selection, retrieval, ordering,
compression, formatting, and lifecycle management. It aims to provide
relevant and reliable information within a model's context constraints.
The term is used broadly in practice and does not refer to one standardized
algorithm.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Model output depends on the information and instructions available at
inference time. Poorly selected or stale context can reduce relevance,
increase cost, confuse instructions, or expose data beyond its intended
scope.

## How it works

An application assembles context from trusted instructions, the current
request, relevant memory or retrieved content, and available tool results.
It filters and orders that material, checks access permissions, and
truncates or summarizes where needed before passing it to the model.

## Practical example

A support assistant can retrieve policy sections relevant to a question,
include their source identifiers, and provide only the permitted excerpts
to the model along with instructions to answer from those sources.

## Common misconceptions

- More context is not always better; irrelevant material can distract or
  exceed limits.
- Context engineering cannot guarantee that a model will follow
  instructions or use evidence correctly.
- Retrieved context should still be checked for relevance, freshness, and
  permissions.
